text: Meridian Regional Health — the same four-hospital system whose Patient Scheduling system was modeled in the CMDB and Discovery course's capstone — now needs its ServiceNow instance to demonstrate real, HIPAA-relevant governance. Leadership wants to know what the platform already gives them, and what their own team still has to build on top of it.

Step one applies Lesson 19's selective-auditing principle directly. Not every field on the Patient Scheduling record carries compliance weight. The fields that do are the patient-adjacent ones: patient name, appointment type, clinic location, and the free-text scheduling notes field — precisely what a HIPAA review would actually ask about.

The deliverable is a short, named list: these specific fields are audited through the Dictionary setting, and these routine ones — sys_id, creation timestamps — deliberately aren't. That list is the actual evidence a reviewer wants: proof auditing was a deliberate decision, not an assumption that everything is already logged.

Step two turns Lesson 18's elevation-logging idea into a real written policy. Before activating security_admin, the admin logs a justification naming the specific ACL they intend to edit and why. Elevation triggers an immediate manager notification, not just a passive log entry. And the justification is reviewed against the actual edit made, after the fact.

That closes the exact gap Lesson 18 warned about: an elevation that happens and gets logged, but that nobody actually reviews. Here, someone is notified the moment it happens, and someone checks afterward that the edit matched what was requested.

Step three documents responsibility honestly. The platform provides the audit logging mechanism, the ACL and role infrastructure, the Elevate Roles mechanism, and encryption and masking capabilities. Meridian's own team owns choosing which fields are patient-adjacent, designing the actual role model, and writing and enforcing the elevation policy.

When leadership asks are we HIPAA compliant now, the honest answer names exactly what's been configured on the platform, while being clear that full compliance also depends on things entirely outside ServiceNow — staff training, physical security, incident response. Chapter 7 opens the course's final stretch: a full capstone security assessment of a real instance, starting with Lesson 22.
